answer.headline: Boston Logan screens highest for expansion among scored New England airports under the base scenario; the screen does not measure terminal capacity.
answer.body:
Among New England census-division airports that clear the base scenario enplanement gate, Boston Logan International (BOS) has the highest expansion screen score at {F94}. Next are Portland International Jetport (PWM, Maine) at {F95} and Tweed New Haven (HVN) at {F96}. The screen flags Tweed as tied with Portland. Those scores are separate findings, so the tie flag does not mean the scores are equal. Bradley International (BDL) at {F97} is not flagged as tied with Tweed. T. F. Green (PVD) at {F98} is flagged as tied with Bradley. Manchester-Boston Regional (MHT) at {F99} is flagged as tied with T. F. Green. Patrick Leahy Burlington International (BTV) at {F100} is flagged as tied with Manchester-Boston. Portland Jetport is not flagged as tied with Boston Logan, and Bradley is not flagged as tied with Tweed.

Each score is calculated. As defined on {F94}, it combines an unconstrained FAA TAF enplanement change (forecast), realized passenger growth (calculated), and home-CBSA per-capita income (calculated). Logan inputs are forecast change {F34}, realized growth {F55}, and income {F67}. Portland inputs are {F44}, {F65}, and {F72}. Tweed inputs are {F38}, {F59}, and {F69}. Bradley inputs are {F32}, {F53}, and {F66}. T. F. Green inputs are {F42}, {F63}, and {F71}. Manchester-Boston inputs are {F40}, {F61}, and {F70}. Burlington inputs are {F36}, {F57}, and {F68}. The TAF change is an FAA forecast, not observed traffic and not unmet demand.

Every scored airport is flagged AIRFIELD_UNKNOWN because no verified FAA capacity rate is on file. The screen therefore does not establish an airfield constraint or a terminal constraint. Tweed is also flagged CARRIER_CONCENTRATION on a calculated largest-carrier seat share of {F76}.

Boston Logan stays first under the equal-weights, demand-only, and momentum-heavy scenarios reported with this screen. The order below Logan does not. Under demand-only, Bradley and T. F. Green rank above Portland. Under momentum-heavy, Tweed ranks above Portland.

Airports below the base gate were not scored. Bangor International ({F4}) is the first airport the screen lists below that gate. A further set of New England airports has no FAA enplanement record and was not scored.

claims.text: Under the base expansion screen, Boston Logan calculated score {F94} is the highest among New England airports the model scored, followed by Portland Jetport {F95}, Tweed New Haven {F96}, Bradley {F97}, T. F. Green {F98}, Manchester-Boston {F99}, and Burlington {F100}.

The screen flags Tweed as tied with Portland, T. F. Green as tied with Bradley, Manchester-Boston as tied with T. F. Green, and Burlington as tied with Manchester-Boston. Portland Jetport is not flagged as tied with Boston Logan, and Bradley is not flagged as tied with Tweed.

Logan score inputs are the FAA TAF enplanement change {F34} (forecast), realized passenger growth {F55} (calculated), and home-CBSA per-capita income {F67} (calculated). The same input types are {F44}, {F65}, and {F72} for Portland; {F38}, {F59}, and {F69} for Tweed; {F32}, {F53}, and {F66} for Bradley; {F42}, {F63}, and {F71} for T. F. Green; {F40}, {F61}, and {F70} for Manchester-Boston; and {F36}, {F57}, and {F68} for Burlington.
Every scored airport carries an AIRFIELD_UNKNOWN flag because no verified FAA capacity rate is available. Tweed also carries a CARRIER_CONCENTRATION flag based on largest-carrier seat share {F76}.

In the equal-weights, demand-only, and momentum-heavy scenarios reported with this screen, Boston Logan remains first. Under demand-only, Bradley and T. F. Green rank above Portland. Under momentum-heavy, Tweed ranks above Portland.
Bangor International, with enplanements {F4}, is the first airport the screen lists as below the base scenario enplanement gate and was not scored.

A high base screen score does not establish that terminal expansion is the indicated project. The score ranks expansion opportunity from forecast passenger growth, recent traffic growth, and market income. It does not measure terminal capacity, unmet demand, fares, or profitability, and the missing capacity rate means a terminal constraint is not established.

assumptions: New England is the Census division of that name, the group the entity resolver returned.
The base screening scenario is the catalog scenario named base. The scenario enplanement gate was left as specified and was not lowered to pull smaller commercial airports into the ranking.
Portland in this result is Portland International Jetport in Maine, the New England airport the screen scored.

Commercial airports the base screen can rank are those that clear the gate. Airports below the gate, and airports with no FAA enplanement record, are outside the scored set rather than assigned a low rank.
limitations: This is a screening rank of expansion opportunity, not a valuation. Costs, debt, airline-agreement economics, and construction risk are not modelled.
The passenger-increase component is an unconstrained FAA TAF forecast, not observed traffic and not unmet demand.

Terminal capacity, gate capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured. NPIAS development need and recent FAA grants shown beside the screen are estimated or observed context only. They are not score inputs and they do not identify a terminal project.
AIRFIELD_UNKNOWN on every scored airport means no verified FAA capacity rate is available, so neither an airfield constraint nor a terminal constraint is established.
Tie flags come from the model. Flagged airports do not have identical scores.
Rank order below Boston Logan changes under the other scenarios the screen reports, so the base order is not robust behind Logan.

Smaller commercial airports in New England were not scored. Bangor is one excluded airport that has an FAA enplanement record. Many other New England fields have no FAA enplanement record and were not scored either.
